text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London struggled to hold above earlier levels but bearish sentiment spilling over from a weak New York market continued to pressure values, traders said. At the close May was down $2.10 at $306.00 per tonne, just above its intraday low of $305.50 per tonne.

There was some interest in the May/August switch, which persistently fluctuated between positive and negative territory, it was added. August was down $1.90 at $305.50 per tonne. Technically the support for May can be pegged at just above $303.00 - an upward trendline dating from last month's trough of $293.50.

Raw sugar futures in New York ended weaker and just of its session lows after a late round of liquidation by speculators, market sources said. With little fresh news to provide impetus, traders were mainly focused on spread activity and position adjustments ahead of March's expiry at the end of the week.

A bout of industry-linked selling dragged prices lower early on, but the market managed to stabilize at mid-session, with aggressive short covering in the May contract offering some support. Keen selling of the March/May switch later in the day dragged the overall market lower.

Most active May ended down 0.07 cent, at 10.83 cents/lb, while spot March fell 0.12 cents, to 10.80 cents/lb. The outer months closed 0.02 to 0.03 cents lower. Traders said the markets direction would hinge in part on May's ability to hold the 10.80 cent level. Additional support was noted at 10.73 to 10.72, followed by 10.60. Upside targets were pegged at today's ceiling of 10.92 cents, followed by 11.19 cents.

THAILAND - Thai Cane and Sugar Board Chief Pramote Vittayasuk projected that the country's sugar output for the 1996/97 (November/October) season will not meet the earlier target of 6.28 million tonnes, tel quel.
Pramote told Reuters that sugar production this season should be close to the 6.03 million tonnes seen in the 1995/96 season. He based his forecast on lower than expected sugar yields.

The Thai Cane and Sugar Board had earlier set the 1996/97 production target at around 6.28 million tonnes of sugar from 60.32 million tonnes of sugar cane, with the yield expected to reach around 103-104 kg of sugar per tonne of cane processed at the end of the crushing season. But as of February 18, the yield had reached only 99.08 kg per tonne, trailing far behind last year's 103.62 kg per tonne.

BRAZIL - Sugar production in January 1997 amounted to 594,900 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 577,900 tonnes. This brought cumulative production in the first three quarters of 1996/97 (May/January) up to 13.977 million tonnes against 12.904 million tonnes in 1995/96.
Total production in 1995/96 amounted to 13.661 million tonnes compared to 12.598 million tonnes in 1994/95 and 10.112 million tonnes in 1993/94.

Total alcohol output in May/January 1996/97 amounted to 13.891 billion litres of which 12.102 billion litres from the Center South (1995/96: 10.907 billion litres) where the campaign ended in December and 1.789 billion litres (1.472 billion litres) from the north/northeast where the campaign is to last until April.

The production of hydrous alcohol reached 9.471 billion litres against 9.447 billion litres while the volume of anhydrous alcohol reached 4.420 billion litres, sharply up from last year's 2.933 billion litres.

Turkey's state sugar holding Turkseker will offer 25,000 tonnes of white sugar for an Iraqi tender to buy 120,000 tonnes under a UN-monitored oil-for-food plan, company manager Selahattin Hun recently said. Hun added Turkseker's new offer price would take into account Iraq's rejection in December of an 50,000 tonne offer, made at $390 per tonne by his company. Results of Iraq's tender could take some time to emerge due to its complexity, traders said.
